question: What language capability should be developed next so generic library APIs can express ordering and equality without adding concrete data-structure implementations?
decision: Add a compile-time-only generic capability model, initially focused on Eq and Ord style constraints, using the existing generic-bound position where practical. Preserve explicit fun(T, T): bool comparator values and validate their signatures through local, imported, namespace-qualified, and re-exported calls.

migration.interface_rule: Exported generic constraints are part of public interface shape and must validate on cache hits; the Rust VM has no runtime constraint representation unless a later decision adds runtime semantics.
migration.direct_input_rule: Direct single-file and ordered direct-multi-file compilation retain existing semantics.
migration.corpus_boundary: Language-only fixtures; no concrete data-structure implementation is part of M6.

comparator_policy: Explicit less: fun(T, T): bool remains supported and its signature must survive imports, namespace aliases, and re-exports.
quantitative_gate: C++ compiler and Rust VM parity where the changed boundary is exercised
explicitly_deferred: Hash protocol and generic hash containers
separate integer type and arbitrary-precision integers
dynamic dispatch, inheritance, overloading, runtime trait objects, and static methods
